artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $p$ be a prime and let $\mathbb{F}_p$ denote the finite field with $p$ elements. For nonempty subsets $A, B \subseteq \mathbb{F}_p$ and a map $\varphi : A \to B$, define the restricted sumset
$$A +_\varphi B := \{\, a + b : a \in A,\ b \in B,\ b \neq \varphi(a)\,\}.$$
Prove or disprove: for every prime $p$, all nonempty subsets $A, B \subseteq \mathbb{F}_p$ with $|A| + |B| < p$, and every injective map $\varphi : A \to B$, one has
$$|A +_\varphi B| \geq |A| + |B| - 3.$$
artifact.status_search_result: The question is a strengthening of the Erdős–Heilbronn conjecture (proved by Dias da Silva–Hamidoune in 1994) to injective maps φ:A→B. Available literature discusses partial results, including a weaker bound |A+_φB| ≥ |A|+|B|-min{|A|,|B|}-1 for arbitrary (not necessarily injective) maps, but no proof of the conjectured |A|+|B|-3 bound under injectivity was located. The problem appears to still be open.
